newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Suspected rebels derail Colombian coal train.
newsitem.headline: Suspected rebels derail Colombian coal train.

text.p: Suspected leftist rebels derailed a train laden with coal in northern Colombia in an attack that could disrupt exports of the mineral for at least five days, police and the state-run Carbones de Colombia coal company said on Wednesday.

They said the dynamite attack occurred late on Tuesday in northern Guajira province along a stretch of a track linking Cerrejon Norte, Latin America's largest open-pit coal mine, with the Caribbean port of Puerto Bolivar.

More than 1,640 feet (500 metres) of track were damaged in the attack, which caused the derailing of 27 railway cars filled with 2,700 metric tons of coal and the spillage of 3,700 gallons (14,000 litres) of diesel fuel.
"This terrorist act will cause delays in the transporation of coal and has a serious impact on operations at the (Cerron Norte) complex," Carbones de Colombia (Carbocol) said in a statement.
A company spokesman told Reuters repair work on the railway was expected to take at least five days and said exports could be delayed until it was completed.

Police blamed the attack on the National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second largest guerrilla group, and said four suspected guerrillas had been arrested on "terrorism" charges. The ELN, founded by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966, specialises in a nationwide campaign of kidnappings and economic sabotage.
Colombia is the world's fourth-largest producer of coal after Australia, South Africa and Poland.

In other developments, a senior army official said authorities had reopened the main highway linking central Colombia with the Atlantic coast early after guerrillas planted landmines along a key section of the roadway and used two hijacked tractor-trailer trucks to serve as makeshift barricades.
Travel along the highway had been suspended since the tractor-trailers, originally believed to be booby-trapped with dynamite charges, were abandoned along the roadway late on Tuesday.
